$comment: The TypeScript half of target selection. rust-output-v1 amendment 005 admits typescript in the target enum and hands every target typescript request and every som.dsl-bundle.v2 bundle with target typescript to this contract. Requests without target, or with target python or rust, are not covered here and keep their responses byte for byte. Amendment 002: rust-output-v1 amendment 006 also admits react and hands target react requests and bundles to react-output-v1, not to this contract. Diagnostics, transport limits and the error envelope are unchanged from som.compiler-api.v1.

x-target-selection.typescript: A som.dsl-bundle.v2 bundle with target typescript, or one diagnostic.
x-target-selection.others: absent, python, rust, react and invalid values: rust-output-v1 api.schema.json x-target-selection, unchanged by this contract. rust-output-v1 amendment 006 admits react and hands it to react-output-v1; this contract's amendment 002 restates its four-target invalid texts in TT01 to TT06.
x-target-selection.before_phase_1: Until a build implements typescript-output-v1 phase 1, target typescript gets the INVALID_SCHEMA refusal of rust-output-v1 CONTRACT.md section 13. No candidate is prepared from such a build.

UNSUPPORTED_TARGET.use: The code rust-output-v1 introduced. For target typescript: a prompt that passes existing validation but is outside TypeScript output phase 1, or a TypeScript bundle whose prompt is outside phase 1. Causes and allowed forms are the scope.json refusals of this contract.

x-check-order: transport limit and JSON parse, including duplicate members
CNL parse or prompt JSON schema
existing compiler-v1 semantic validation, unchanged (this already refuses a v3 filter field named limit or offset, compiler-v1 amendment 003)
TypeScript profile, only when target is typescript, in the scope.json refusal_order (UNSUPPORTED_TARGET)
planning, with SCOPE_TOO_LARGE for a TypeScript DSL over 12 files or over 64 blocks in total, or an assemble envelope over 2097152 bytes
x-assemble-check-order: transport limit, JSON parse and envelope schema
bundle version dispatch: only a bundle whose version member is the string som.dsl-bundle.v2 continues; every other bundle keeps the compiler-v1 order and result unchanged

target dispatch: a bundle whose target member is the string typescript continues below; target rust follows rust-output-v1; target react follows react-output-v1 (rust-output-v1 amendment 006, this contract's amendment 002); any other value is INVALID_SCHEMA at /bundle/target after the members and version checks of the rust-output-v1 check_schema order
bundle schema som.dsl-bundle.v2.typescript in the rust-output-v1 check_schema order, and at most 64 blocks in total (INVALID_SCHEMA at the failing pointer)
hashes: prompt_sha256, dsl_sha256, then payload_sha256 = H({version,target,prompt,dsl,assets}) (BUNDLE_HASH_MISMATCH)
asset descriptors equal the active TypeScript manifest (ASSET_HASH_MISMATCH at /bundle/assets)
TypeScript profile (UNSUPPORTED_TARGET at /bundle/prompt plus the scope.json pointer)
catalog and composition: every block id is an admitted ts. block in the frozen order for the prompt (INVALID_COMPOSITION at the block id)

x-manifest.shared_with_rust: grammar, compiler_contract, selection_policy, literal_policy, serializer and semantic_contracts equal the Rust manifest's descriptors for the same build.
x-manifest.target_contract: id som.typescript-output-contract.v1; sha256 is the canonical hash of the sealed receipt's files map, as for rust-output-v1.
x-manifest.catalog: id som.typescript-catalog.v1; descriptor {id, sha256} with the SHA-256 of the bytes of catalog/typescript-catalog.v1.json as embedded in som-targets.
x-manifest.block_library: id som.typescript-block-library.v1; descriptor {id, sha256} with the SHA-256 of the concatenated text of the TypeScript renderer sources that hold the block bodies, in the order som-targets/src/typescript/mod.rs lists them, as the Rust BLOCK_LIBRARY_TEXT.
x-manifest.backend: id som.typescript-backend.v1; sha256 = H({"version": "som.typescript-backend.v1", "files": {path: SHA-256 of the file text}}), the formula of the Rust backend descriptor. The files map has every source that decides the TypeScript bundle and its files, keyed by som-rs-relative path (som-targets/...): every file under som-targets/src/typescript/, plus the shared som-targets/Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/main.rs and src/profile.rs. Shared files appear in both backend maps, so an edit to one changes both descriptors: it needs an amendment of both contracts and is recorded as a bundle compatibility break for both targets (rust-output-v1 CONTRACT.md section 13).
